clean_claim:
Two-thirds or more of the api/ tests, migrations and scripts look publishable as-is.

Clean with medium-high confidence:
- All 14 other api/* files. The cert is Supabase's public CA, with no private key. bun.lock has no auth tokens. The Dockerfile label points at the private repo URL, which will simply be outdated after the move.
- About 140 of the 181 migrations: the legacy 0000–0027 files and the 2026-05 to 2026-09 schema files outside the 20260519T160000–20260520T240000 band, other than the low-level lore and emoji or path notes flagged. Their INSERTs are synthetic: platform zero-UUID rows, fake tx hashes in the payout fixture repair, and set-based ledger reversals with no real ids.
- Roughly 500 of the 615 test files: all non-doctrine route, unit, integration and contract tests, apart from the specific lines flagged, and about 95 product-doctrine tests (Promises, canon shape, KIN, rings, loops, pyramid, rights, love-consent, joy and love-bomb product). All credential-shaped literals I checked were placeholders ("secret", "fixture", *.invalid, *.example, reserved IPs, a1/b2 seeds). Fixtures (crown vectors, provider evaluations, launch-core journey) are synthetic.
- About 45 of the 80 scripts: generic e2e and payout harnesses, x402 proof tools after review of the dev keys and treasury address, migration helpers after the username fix, and new-migration, sign-*, inbox-send-self and walls.

I found no live secret values: no real API tokens, JWTs, Stripe keys, private keys other than the public Hardhat dev keys, mnemonics or passwords. Third-party issues: none found. There are no vendored or copyrighted texts in scope beyond cited research summaries. The CC BY-SA mentions concern the project's own specs.
limits:
- **Coverage.** I did not read all 615 test files line by line. Every regex hit was judged in context. Every migration header in the relational band was read, along with the bodies of the key ones. Files with no hits were sampled by header only (all 152 doctrine-test headers, all script headers). Relational content that uses none of the searched vocabulary could still remain, though I think that is unlikely.
- **Decisions this scope cannot make.** Many flagged tests pin content that lives in api/src, docs/ and docs/agenttool.jsonld, which are outside this scope. Whether those tests can go public depends on what happens to that content. If the relational docs stay private, the tests that read them will fail in the public tree, and roughly 45 doctrine tests also read machine-local absolute paths or the owner's private ~/.claude files, so they can never pass outside that one Mac.
- **Migration journal.** Migrations are checksum-frozen, and the runners refuse a journaled filename whose source is missing. Withholding the 26+ relational migrations, or splitting the 4 mixed DDL+seed ones, keeps a fresh public DB working but makes the public tree unusable against the production journal. The owner needs to pick between a private overlay of the withheld files and a new public migration lineage. I verified the runner rule from migrations/README.md only, not from the runner code.
- **Verified vs inferred.** Text content, line numbers and that the Hardhat keys are the well-known defaults are verified. Whether the Supabase project ref, the Fly origin and the treasury address count as sensitive is a judgment call. So is whether the persona CLI can be rewritten generically, and whether the future date in the 1:1 letters test is personal.
- **What I kept out of this output.** I loaded the private denylist terms only to apply them, and none appear here. Path segments that are denylist terms are masked with `*`. I did not copy the owner's email, the project ref, persona emails or quoted directives.
- **Not done.** The api/src tree, the mechanical gitleaks run (running separately) and git history are outside this scope. The planned public repo is a fresh snapshot without history, so history was not reviewed.
